thread.title: Interstellar object spotted 'bleeding' mysterious metals that defy science - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Interstellar object spotted 'bleeding' mysterious metals that defy science - NewsBreak

author: Peter Rubinstein
title: Interstellar object spotted 'bleeding' mysterious metals that defy science - NewsBreak
text:
By Peter Rubinstein ,
1 hours ago
A mysterious celestial body speeding through the solar system and shedding metals was captured in July by the Very Large Telescope in Chile, one of five developed by NASA to detect objects that might collide with the Earth.
The 20-inch telescope, located in the Rio Hurtado Valley, was performing its nightly survey when it picked up something moving at such a high speed that it could not have been orbiting our sun - meaning it must have come from interstellar space. It is the third such object ever recorded by terrestrial telescopes, and was described by researchers as "extremely puzzling."
Subsequent observations of the speedy object, named 3I/ATLAS, found that it contained nickel but not iron, suggesting that the metal was created from a never-before-seen chemical process . "We just cracked open the door to a whole new world of chemistry that we never had access to before," Thomas Puzia, an astronomer at the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile whose team analyzed the telescope's observation, told Smithsonian Magazine .
The object's abundance of nickel and ratio of carbon dioxide to water, which was discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), were also especially unique.
"Its CO2-to-water ratio in the coma... is among the highest ever seen in any comet," said Martin Cordiner, an astronomer at the Catholic University of America and the lead investigator of the JWST's findings.
3I/ATLAS will reach its perihelion, the point on its trajectory of closest distance to the sun, around Oct. 30 before it arcs back around the star and careens into outer space.
A model that was created based on the object's velocity relative to the sun found that one possible reason for its chemical composition is the amount of time it has been traveling. According to the model, 3I/ATLAS may have been flying through space for seven billion years or more.
"If this object has passed through the [galactic] disk a few times, it probably passed through interstellar clouds, probably passed through star-forming regions where there's new giant stars being born, supernovae going off," Cordiner said.
"It's probably passed through a whole range of different environments."
The only other observable interstellar objects to have passed through our solar system were 'Oumuamua' in 2017 and 21/Borisov in 2019 The research team also surmised that its unique structure may have formed from rare metal compounds, high levels of carbon oxides or small hot spots on its surface.
The only other observable interstellar objects to have passed through our solar system were "Oumuamua," discovered in 2017, and 21/Borisov, discovered in 2019.
It had been approaching the area near the constellation Sagittarius near the center of the Milky Way, NASA said in a statement.
In measuring the object's nickel-to-iron ratio at different distances from the sun, researchers hope to determine whether 3I/ATLAS is truly a one-of-a-kind celestial body.
Their findings could alter the scientific community's foundational understanding of how comets are formed, and how their metals react and change in the farthest reaches of space.
